questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I have been living in Delhi _______ April 1995.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'since'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given blank needs a **preposition of time.**
 
• We use **since **to refer back to a previous point in time.
 
• Thus, **option 1 **is the correct answer.

***Correct sentence - ****I have been living in Delhi **since **April 1995.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **With **as a **preposition **means ‘in the same place as someone or something’ or ‘accompanying’.
 
• **For **as a preposition is used to talk about a purpose or a reason for something.
 
• Through as a preposition is used to refer to a period of time from start to finish.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

They opened the gates to the theatre at 6 pm sharp.

options.text: The gates to the theatre were opened by them at 6 pm sharp.
The gates to the theatre had been opened by them at 6 pm sharp.
The gates to the theatre were kept open by them at 6 pm sharp.
The gates to the theatre were being opened by them at 6 pm sharp.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**The gates to the theatre were opened by them at 6 pm sharp.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in active voice. As per the question we have to change it into passive voice.
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject + past participle + Object (Active voice)
 
• Subject (objective case) + were + past participle + by Object (subjective case) (Passive voice)
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *They built large gardens. (Active voice)*
 
• *Large gardens were built by them. (Passive voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is ‘they’.
 
• The object of the given subject is ‘the gates’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• opened will be changed to were opened.
 
• The **pronoun they **is changed to **them**.
 
• Correct sentence - The gates to the theatre were opened by them at 6 pm sharp.

questions.question:

The secretary has __fewer work__ to do than I have yet he complains.
questions.solution:

• There is an error in the **quantifier **used in the underlined part. 
 
• **Fewer is a quantifier** used with **plural nouns** - *Better cycle routes would mean **fewer **cars and **fewer **accidents.*
 
• For an **uncountable noun **like **work **we need to use the **quantifier less. **
 
• Thus, the underlined part should be replaced with **less work. **
 
• This makes **option 2 **the correct answer.

questions.question:

I said to my friend, " Why didn't you answer my phone calls?"

options.text: I asked my friend why she hadn't answered my phone calls.
I asked my friend why she hasn't answered my phone calls.
I asked my friend why she isn't answering my phone calls.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an interrogative sentence. 
 
• While changing the narration of an interrogative sentence, we need to follow these steps
 
 
• the reported speech will start with *why*
 
• The reporting verb said is changed into asked or enquired__.
 
• The second person 'you' will be changed into she.
 
• The tense of the given sentence is present tense (answer) which changes to past tense (answered).
 
• **Didn't** is changed to **hadn't**. (past indefinite tense changes to past definite tense) 
 
 
 
• Eventually, we will get the final sentence-* *I asked my friend why she hadn't answered my phone calls.

questions.question:
**Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them contains a grammatical error. Select the option that has the error.**

It's been many years have I left Mumbai and settled in Delhi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'have I left'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The erroneous part is **have I left.**
 
• The given sentence can be divided into two clauses - 
 
 
• the **independent clause - ***It's been many years*
 
• the **subordinate clause - ***I left Mumbai and settled in Delhi.*
 
 
 
• To join the two clause we need to use a **subordinating conjunction **instead of the **determiner that.**
 
• So, the part with the error makes **option 2 **the correct answer. 
 
• If we use the **subordinating conjunction since, **the sentence will be correct. 

***Correct sentence - ****It's been many years **since **I left Mumbai and settled in Delhi.*

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The master of the house came in and passing rapidly through the dining-room went to his own room.

B. I was hurrying away to my own little retreat upstairs when I heard a sound.

C. The street door creaked upon its hinges and heavy feet made the made the whole flight of stairs to shake.

D. I could see that his restless eyes were in incessant motion behind his full-sized spectacles and his long, thin nose was like a knife blade.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**B, C, A , D**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some __grammatical or contextual__ connections between them. Also, the first sentence of a passage is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. 

__
 
• Sentence B is the independent sentence and sets the tone of the passage.
 
• So, sentence B is the first sentence after rearrangement. It talks about how the subject (I) was going to their room when they heard a sound. 
 
• Sentence C describes the source of the sound and the following events related to it. Hence, C follows B.__
 
• Sentence A which describes how the noise was being made by the master of the house should come after sentence C, to maintain continuity on the topic. 
 
• Sentence D is the concluding statement of the passage as it talks about how the subject viewed the person who came in. 

Thus, the correct order after rearrangement is option 4 i.e. B, C, A , D.

So, the correct paragraph is : ***(******B) I was hurrying away to my own little retreat upstairs when I heard a sound. (C) The street door creaked upon its hinges and heavy feet made the made the whole flight of stairs to shake. (A) The master of the house came in and passing rapidly through the dining-room went to his own room. (D) I could see that his restless eyes were in incessant motion behind his full-sized spectacles and his long, thin nose was like a knife blade.***

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

My teacher is encouraging me to improve my performance in the SAT examination.

options.text: I am being encouraged by my teacher to improve my performance in the SAT exam.
I had been encouraged by my teacher to improve my performance in the SAT exam.
I was being encouraged by my teacher to improve my performance in the SAT exam.
I am encouraged by my teacher to improve my performance in the SAT exam.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****I am being encouraged by my teacher to improve my performance in the SAT exam**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **active voice.** As per the question we have to change it into** passive voice.**
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• **Subject + to be (is) + present participle + Object (Active voice)**
 
• **Subject (objective case) + **to be (is) + being +** past participle + by Object (subjective case) (Passive voice)**
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *My boss is giving many assignments. (Active voice)*
 
• *Many assignments are being given by my boss. (Passive voice)*
 
 
 
• The **subject **of the given sentence is ‘my teacher’.
 
• The **object **of the given subject is ‘me’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• **is encouraging **will be changed to **am being encouraged**.
 
• The **me **in active voice changes to **I **in passive voice.
 
• Correct sentence - I am being encouraged by my teacher to improve my performance in the SAT exam.

questions.question: "The cycle continues. It's a vicious circle." The writer calls it a vicious circle because:

• In the second paragraph of the passage it has been stated - 
 
 
• *"We're society of waste and overconsumption,"says Emmanuel Vallee, organiser of the Repair Cafe Paris, which typically sees around 25 people attending per event, including some online, since it launched in May 2019. "We throw things away that we don't need to and buy new gadgets before exploring the possibility of repair. The cycle continues. It's a vicious circle."*
